title: shipping traffic via strait hormuz stays below 10 day average data shows 2026 09 09
text:
SINGAPORE, Sept 9 (Reuters) - Six ​commodity vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, down from ‌nine a day earlier and below the 10-day average of about 12, preliminary shipping data showed on Wednesday.
The figures exclude any vessels that might have crossed the strait with their Automatic Identification System transponders turned ​off to avoid detection.
Of the six vessels, five were entering and one was ​exiting, initial data from shiptracker Kpler showed at 0200 GMT. They included ⁠one Panamax and one intermediate tanker.
The chokepoint at the southern tip of the Gulf prior ​to the start of the Iran war on February 28 typically handled about 125 large, commercial ​vessels per day, including oil tankers and natural gas carriers. The traffic accounted for some 20% of the world’s daily crude oil and liquefied natural gas supply.
A U.S. blockade of Iran-related shipping has halted Iranian ​crude oil exports since it was reimposed in mid-July.
The U.S.-Israeli war ​on Iran intensified on Tuesday when Tehran-backed Houthis in Yemen launched strikes on several Saudi Arabian cities. In addition, ‌U.S. ⁠forces hit multiple Iranian oil tankers and Iran struck a U.S. base in Jordan.
The heightened conflict and continued disruption of energy markets drove oil prices above $100 a barrel on Tuesday.
According to a report by marine intelligence firm Marisks, U.S. forces rendered inoperable five Iran-linked crude ​oil tankers, the M/T ​Kaviz, Charminar, Horizon 1, ⁠Riesco and Derya.
Four of the vessels were reportedly struck in the Gulf of Oman, outside the Strait of Hormuz, and one near ​Kharg Island, Iran's most important export terminal, the report added.
In the ​Red Sea, where ⁠Houthi militants have announced a blockade of Saudi-related shipping, 25 commodity vessels transited the Bab el-Mandeb strait on Tuesday. Of these, 11 vessels entered and 14 exited.
This compares with an average ⁠of around ​27 ships going through Bab el-Mandeb over the last ​10 days.
Among the vessels travelling through the strait were two Suezmax tankers, eight Aframax tankers and one Very ​Large Crude Carrier.
